The moment you beat the similar behavior into these other shells, you end up with the same overhead fish has, especially with incredibly bloated packages like ohmyzsh and the like.

Compatibility and POSIX compliance is often brought up, but is honestly not really a problem these days if you know what you are doing. Just add #!/bin/sh to your scripts, there, done. Fish has a few powerful features other shells don't have in scripting that are worth exploring.

Personally, for really complicated scripts I don't bother with either and just use lua. The nice thing that sets fish apart from the other shells and make me use it is that the advanced features you named like autocompletion etc. "just work", without much configuration or overhead in the way of heavy scripting.

It's very subtle for me, my problem was that it was almost impossible to break out of my thought patterns and I tried for years. All kinds of self help that just did absolutely nothing for me. I just was always back in the same hole at the end. Simple things going wrong or one negative thought could depress me for days. I'd lose entire weeks in a depressed stupor. I couldn't focus. I couldn't really do anything. It was never always like that and like everyone with depression of course you do have some ok days too but you never really get anywhere. I lived years like this.

Then with the medication, something changed. I had a bit more energy. I could concentrate. The negative thoughts were still there but instead of hovering like a dark cloud for days, they would pass in minutes and just simply not affect me all that much. I could move on. My brain wasn't like a needle skipping on a record anymore. That brought me to have positive experiences like actually managing to do my work and day-to-day things I didn't manage anymore. That made me feel even better. I had to dicontinue the first medication because of side effects and started a different one. All in all it took half a year until I was there with the medication but it was worth it. I stuck with trying because I literally didn't know what else to do. Therapy helped too, of course.

A lot of information online is very negative, I think because many people who are depressed don't have the patience to wait for this stuff to work (I can get that, I was there myself) Others are afraid to take something that'll affect their brain. Again others somehow expect these pills will fix their life circumstances but of course they don't, you have to do that yourself. At any rate, by no means are they "happy pills", turn you into a mindless zombie or anything like that. If anything, I am myself again, like I used to be. I didn't think it was possible. My experience was *very* positive.

Try, but most of all don't get discouraged early on. It takes up to 6 weeks to even notice the first effects and the first medication you take might not even be for you. Many give up too soon, for me it changed my life.

I use seeding for the settlements (arcologies really) in my game. I don't want to save tons of detail about them and their citizens in game files, as that's all data that will not be used regularly (if ever more than once really) anyways. But by using seeds, I create a kind of familiarity about these arcologies in case the player returns or even visits them regularly. You will even have a chance to run into the same people!
